title: It's difficult to add a label to the index selector
body:
like 'sort by'

I think that adding a label should be allowed by the widget same way as refinementList allows header.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/976175/11136336/c3bb22cc-89ad-11e5-9e03-74ede4c4fb32.png)

comments.body: Cannot do something like https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/master/dev/index.html#L45-L46 ?

in your example the 'for' attribute doesn't match the input (should have a name/id) and it breaks the bootstrap structure label.control-label + div > input.form-control.
So we still can do some magic but I'had the feeling that is wansn't handy enough
Hmm.. I was wrong, structure is good so the only remaining problem is 'for' attribute of the label.

> the only remaining problem is 'for' attribute of the label.

Yes indeed, and we'll have the same issue for the `numericalSelector`. Easy to add the `label`, but I'm still worried about the way we'll generate the underlying `id`s to bind the `for`.

I'm not sure I get the issue. Why can't we do a ``? Anyway, we do not have to be Bootstrap compliant (at least, not for v1.0.0). If we really need to have the select outside of the label, I would simply allow passing a `selectId` option to the widget, and let the user correctly set the same `for` on the label.

Input inside the label is wrong on both semantical and W3c aspect.
"we do not have to be Bootstrap compliant" <- No, we have to be compliant with EVERYTHING (so, seek an destroy this kind of small incompatibility).
Your proposition break the logic (User just added tittle of his facets, he won't understand why labels are not supported for a simple select) + it's made to be easy so if I have to read the doc to make a valid markup, it's not cool.

> Input inside the label is wrong on both semantical and W3c aspect.

Just for the sake of it, can you link to the W3C issue? I only found this: http://www.w3.org/TR/html401/interact/forms.html#h-17.9 and they actually say that one or the other is feasible. Maybe I miss a link
ok right, it works for w3C.. It's still ugly and doesn't make much sense semantically but ok.

> Input inside the label is wrong on both semantical and W3c aspect.

Hmm, that's how Bootstrap does it for checkbox/radio. Wrapping an input in a label works the same as linking them through `for`/`id`, but this can actually be really helpful when styling.

> Your proposition break the logic (User just added tittle of his facets, he won't understand why labels are not supported for a simple select)+ it's made to be easy so if I have to read the doc to make a valid markup, it's not cool.

Oh ok, you mean we should provide the API directly in the widget to add a label, to stay consistent with the fact that we already provide a way to add headers. Sorry, I did not get that. But yeah, that could be a nice improvement.

But still... I'm not confortable with adding too many markup from the widget. If I take the Bootstrap example of doing selects in form this is: ``` html
``` Which will translate in instantsearch to ``` html
``` ``` javascript search.addWidget( instantsearch.widgets.hitsPerPageSelector({ container: '#selector-menu', options: [{},{}, ...], selectId: 'selector', cssClasses: { root: 'form-control' } }) ); ``` I've only added the `selectId` option, that should add an `id` to the `select`, so it is correctly bound to the `label`. I don't think we should wrap the `select` in a `label` from the widget (not anybody would want a wrapped element). I'm not sure we should automatically add a label before the select (users not using Bootstrap might want it somewhere else, or wrapped in their own div).

> I've only added the selectId option, that should add an id to the select, so it is correctly bound to the label. I don't think we should wrap the select in a label from the widget (not anybody would want a wrapped element).

Yes me too, for other widgets we do have some automatic labels but they are in a template you can change. While here you cannot change the structure once done.

> I've only added the selectId option, that should add an id to the select,

I like it so, simple API change for power users.
wfm
moved to #679

I understand the will not to add too much markup from the widget itself, but I have a question then: how is one supposed to hide the `<label>` when `autoHideContainer` is set to `true` on the widget and the search returns no hits?

Just had an idea: what about imitating what's been done with HTML?
We don't want a hard-coded `<label>` inside each widget, but we could have a generic `label` widget that is given a reference to the widget it relates to using a `for` option/prop.

We should then have a way to synchronize the `display: none` (and the name/id for its real `for` attribute) between the widget and its label?

Something along those lines:

``` javascript
let sortSelector = instantsearch.widgets.sortBySelector(...);
search.addWidget(instantsearch.widgets.label({ container: '#sortby-wrapper', for: sortSelector }))
search.addWidget(sortSelector);
```

Would that work?

> how is one supposed to hide the <label> when autoHideContainer is set to true

Yes you're right; we need to find something.
@olance Good point about the `autoHideContainer`. The previous suggested solution of `selectId` won't cut it.

@olance about your proposition yes it would work but it would be cool if we could find a simpler way to do it because it look like a lot of code for a simple `<label>`

I would want to be able as a user to say `{label: 'select smg' }` in the option of the sort by selector.

If anyone has an idea on how to do it without breaking things for people that would be cool

The original request from @Shipow makes sense as a user perspective:

> I think that adding a label should be allowed by the widget same way as refinementList allows header.

Hmmm yes, it's simpler though limited. Unless we have a template option to which the `label` option value is passed so that it can be placed at any other place than the default one without having to create a custom widget just for that.

Or "as a user, I would like to be able to choose the label's place without having to create a whole new widget for it" ^^
